job.direction:
EDIT THE SUPPLIED TRANSPARENT NINE-CELL PRODUCTION ATLAS as a material/style finish pass. Preserve its exact orthographic constructions, positions, projected axes, door openings, scale and crop. Do not create a new layout or redistribute the nine objects. Change only material colour, gentle broad painted shading, and modest roof styles that fit those same constructions. The supplied3x3 square atlas already has the correct three equal rows and columns; every input pixel position remains at the same normalized output position. Keep the large empty upper space of each cell, do not centre the silhouette in that space. Actual ground-centre in EVERY cell is exactly(128,192),75%cellheight. Garden vertices in each normalized256cell are BACK(128,140.8),RIGHT(230.4,192),FRONT(128,243.2),LEFT(25.6,192); fence feet sit on those exact lines, all groundlines slopes±.5. Do not change the slopes, garden positions or widths. Every cell's front garden vertex remains95%down that cell, including the last row, so the last row front garden corners approach95%down the bottom row rather than floating at its centre. FIRSTSIX personneldoors22.4pxheight, storeys32px; LASTTHREE personneldoors11.2pxheight,storeys16px. Preserve the physically smaller doors and windows in the larger two-tile parcels of the bottom row exactly. Rotation0 doors, path and gates face LOWER-LEFT. Redraw the architectural entrance orientation by swapping the two world axes while keeping the same2:1 camera and northwest lighting; never horizontally mirror lighting or rotate the plot off-grid. Retain guide construction without its small white calibration ticks. Genuine transparent background and cell gutters. Quiet broad slate/terracotta roofs, plaster/timber/brick/stone facades, low simple fences and2or3soft shrub masses. No roof tile marks, brick joints, woodgrain, flower dots, foliage speckle, outlines, tiny lettering, lawn texture, elevated yard slabs, people, swatches or gridlines. Match canonical muted palette, particularly neutral muted lawn#91a77a, creamplaster#e3d7b7, brick#b1846c, terracotta#a76f51, slate#697780. This is a geometry-preserving finish pass over the supplied exact measured constructions; do not substitute another camera, vertical layout or feature scale.
Dry muted sand#c6b48b and foliage#899265, sparse broad dry shrubs; no saturated orange terrain.
CRITICAL TRANSPARENCY: Garden lawn/grass is EMPTY TRANSPARENT SPACE. Keep house, paths, low fence, individual broad shrubs only. Native world terrain must show underneath; no opaque green garden plate, ground fill, soil/sand/snow plane, slab or grassy pixels between these objects. Remove the reference lawn entirely without shifting the garden fence-foot vertices or architecture. Transparent garden holes are intentional and required, not an incomplete illustration.
Use this approved house design as a climate-only edit: retain exact architecture, source positions, measured camera, door/window scale, roofs and fences. Change broad plant masses to muted dry shrubs and light to warm restrained desert light. Native sandy garden ground remains EMPTY alpha0; no sand/soil plate, grass, partly opaque lawn noise or snowy fill. Keep only architecture, fences, gate, path and broad shrubs. Broad quiet roofs with no tiles, and stone facades without masonry grids.

prompt:
Fixed orthographic 2:1 dimetric camera: ground edges at +26.565 and -26.565 degrees, vertical walls, two visible facades, no perspective convergence.
Lock every building, roof ridge, garden boundary, fence, court and yard to the same two ground axes. No in-plot yaw, diagonal rotation, camera tilt or camera rotation. An alternate entrance orientation swaps the two grid axes; it never rotates a building off-grid.
Quiet hand-painted miniature architecture with clean silhouettes, broad roof and wall colour masses, restrained warm materials, northwest daylight and soft contact shadows.
A consistent world scale: one tile is 16 metres square. A person is 1.75m tall; ordinary personnel doors are 2.1m high and 0.95m wide; storeys are 3m; windows are about 1.2m high; low fences are 1.2m. Vehicle loading bays are 4.2m high and visibly distinct from personnel doors.
Bigger buildings gain additional rooms, wings, floors and repeated bays at the SAME human scale. Never enlarge doors, windows, people, garden fences or benches to fill a bigger parcel.
Designed to remain recognizable at Region 0.5x and Town 1x: distinctive roofline, clear facade shading, a few large openings and broad planted clusters. No individual bricks, roof tiles, woodgrain scratches, tiny lettering, tiny flower dots, dense crate grids, fine handrails, thin window mullions or decorative speckle.
Preserve useful large identifiers such as loading sheds, silos, greenhouses, chimneys, awnings and sports surfaces. No people as decorative scale filler, no text or logos.
Use the supplied semantic muted material swatches across all families; maintain broad light and shaded facades within those hues. Give each identity a distinct roofline or one large identifying mass, with restrained slate, terracotta, foliage, ochre or burgundy accents. Recognition at Town size must come from silhouette and broad colour blocks, not tiny ornaments or texture.
Genuine transparent background, isolated complete sprites with generous transparent gutters. No scenery outside the parcel, no backdrop cards or opaque plinth. In house gardens leave every unpaved lawn area transparent so native world terrain shows through; retain paths, fences and individual shrubs. Courts, pools and other necessary built surfaces retain their material.
Production 3x3 atlas, exactly 9 slots in row-major order; each cell is a registered architectural cutout at the stated parcel scale, not a close-up of the building. Follow each slot's parcel-to-cell calibration: equal footprints share one pixel-to-metre scale; larger footprints have proportionally smaller doors in the normalized cell so they render at the same world height. Do not give different footprint tiers equal door pixel heights. Do not independently fit each building's bounding box.
Physical ground registration in every 256px square cell: parcel centre is (128.0,192.0), independent of alpha bounds, shadows, roof height and planting. Around that centre project east/north/up metres with x=(east-north)*2 and y=(east+north)-height*2 in world pixels, then multiply by 256/(48*footprint). The inset architectural/garden envelope is at most 10m*footprint square; its exact 2:1 ground vertices are (128.0,138.7), (234.7,192.0), (128.0,245.3), (21.3,192.0). The full 16m*footprint parcel is native world terrain and extends beyond this cutout cell; do not shrink its physical metre scale or paint a full-parcel opaque diamond to fit the cell. Register the actual ground centre, never the silhouette bottom or contact-shadow extremity. Keep all complete architecture and planting inside the transparent cell with filtering gutters.
Warm dusty sand, pale stone and plaster, terracotta and sparse dry planting; preserve every physical dimension.
Canonical desert material swatches: plaster #e3d7b7; stone #c7bca5; brick #b1846c; timber #997a5b; slate #697780; terracotta #a76f51; glass #769493; metal #6c7878; ink #4b5954; cream #f0e9d6; ochre #c2a269; burgundy #996b63; paving #cdc6ae; path #d8cfb2; water #658f9c; ground #c6b48b; foliage #899265. These are restrained painted colour targets, with soft light/shade variation, not saturated replacements.
